name: Comdb2
tagline: Bloomberg's clustered relational database with optimistic concurrency and synchronous replication.
description: Comdb2 is the relational database Bloomberg has run in production since the mid-2000s and open-sourced in 2016. It combines a SQLite-derived SQL frontend with a heavily modified Berkeley DB storage layer, and clusters replicate synchronously so any node can serve reads and accept writes with serializable or snapshot isolation via optimistic concurrency. It supports stored procedures in Lua, triggers and queues for event delivery, online schema changes and table partitioning. It is battle-tested at Bloomberg scale, but outside Bloomberg the community, documentation and tooling are small.

scale.notes: Full-replica clusters with synchronous replication; partitioning and remote-table queries for larger datasets.

strengths: Synchronous replication with serializable isolation across the cluster
Optimistic concurrency lets any node accept writes
Online schema changes without blocking traffic
Built-in queues and Lua triggers for event-driven designs
Two decades of production use at Bloomberg
weaknesses: Small external community and few third-party tools or drivers
Not wire-compatible with MySQL or PostgreSQL
Sparse documentation compared with mainstream databases
Optimistic concurrency causes retries on hot rows
useCases: Event delivery via database queues and triggers
Clusters needing strong consistency across nodes
notIdealFor: Teams needing broad ORM and tooling support
